articles.title: Left-arm taking over: Zaheer Khan appointed as CSK head coach after Stephen Fleming's exit
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) champions Chennai Super Kings (CSK) on Monday appointed former India pacer Zaheer Khan as their head .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) champions Chennai Super Kings (CSK) on Monday appointed former India pacer Zaheer Khan as their head coach."Left Arm 'Taking' Over! Welcoming Zaheer Khan as the Head Coach of Chennai Super Kings," CSK said in a post on X.Zaheer Khan will take over as Chennai Super Kings' head coach from Stephen Fleming, who held the position from 2009 to 2026. CSK parted ways with Fleming after failing to make the play-offs for a third season in a row.Zaheer played 92 Tests, 200 ODIs and 17 T20Is for India. He was India's highest wicket-taker during their 2011 ODI World Cup-winning campaign, taking 21 wickets.Since retiring from the IPL in 2017, Zaheer has worked with several teams. He represented three IPL teams, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Mumbai Indians and Delhi Capitals, before joining MI as their Director of Cricket Operations ahead of the 2019 season. He later became the franchise's head of global development.Zaheer was named Lucknow Super Giants' mentor for IPL 2025 but left the franchise ahead of the following season.As a player, Zaheer made 100 IPL appearances and took 102 wickets at an average of 27.27. articles.title: 'Pujara used to irritate us': Tim Paine recalls Australia's biggest headache against India
articles.summary: Cricket News: Puducherry: Former Australia Test captain Tim Paine is currently working with Australia A, who will take on India A in the first four-day game in Pudu.
articles.body: Puducherry: Former Australia Test captain Tim Paine is currently working with Australia A, who will take on India A in the first four-day game in Puducherry starting Tuesday. With Australia preparing for the next Border-Gavaskar Trophy (Jan-Mar 2027), Paine spoke to TOI about the importance of exposing young players to Indian conditions, the next generation of Australian bowlers and his memories of facing Cheteshwar Pujara and Rishabh Pant.How important are these ‘A’ tours for Australia?Very important. That’s why we’re investing quite a lot of time and resources into getting the next group of cricketers over here, whether it’s through Australia A, the MRF Foundation or some of the work we do with younger players. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is a really important one for us. It’s been more than 20 years since we’ve won it in India. The more times we can get here, acclimatise to the weather, food and different batting and bowling conditions and develop game plans, the better.India A have players like Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan. How do you see the contest?We want to see how our players adapt to them. There’s a lot of footage available, but if it was as simple as saying, ‘This is his weakness and this is how you get him out’, they wouldn’t be the player they are now. It’s an amazing experience for our young bowlers to bowl to players of that quality in these conditions.Which Indian batter was hardest to dismiss during your captaincy?(Cheteshwar) Pujara. He was hard to get out. He had great concentration and discipline and was tough. He used to irritate us. We were just trying to get him out. Pat Cummins eventually figured him out a bit and got him caught behind.How do you remember Rishabh Pant’s famous Gabba innings?I loved the way he came to Australia and played, how aggressive and confident he was. That’s something we’re trying to instil in this young group, the belief that you can go out and change games. That’s what Rishabh did against high-class bowlers. He threw them off their lines and lengths and put them under pressure. It was a great way to play, and a lot of the time I try and encourage our players to do the same thing.Are you surprised Pant is not part of India’s white-ball set-up?I haven’t watched enough of his white-ball cricket to say. I know his IPL over the last couple of years hasn’t been brilliant, but if he’s playing well, he could be playing in most white-ball teams around the world. It’s probably about capturing that form again and taking his red-ball cricket into white-ball cricket. There’s no reason why someone as skilled and talented as him, if he’s playing well, wouldn’t be a fantastic white-ball player.What are Australia’s chances in the next BGT?I think Australia have a good chance. Batting-wise, we probably haven’t scored as many runs as we would have liked in the last couple of summers, but there are still some high-quality players in the team. Either way, Australia will be very well prepared and I can’t see any reason why the Aussies can’t win.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'MS Dhoni obviously plays a key role': CSK reveal thinking behind Zaheer Khan appointment as coach
articles.summary: Cricket News: Chennai: Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s pinnacle as India captain was the 2011 World Cup triumph, and Zaheer Khan was one of that campaign’s unsung heroes. Hi.
articles.body: Chennai: Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s pinnacle as India captain was the 2011 World Cup triumph, and Zaheer Khan was one of that campaign’s unsung heroes. His joint-highest tally of 21 wickets in the tournament, alongside Pakistan skipper Shahid Afridi, and his opening spell of 5-3-6-1 in the final against Sri Lanka at the Wankhede are not celebrated as much as some of the other performances from that campaign.Now, as Dhoni enters the final chapter of his playing career, he has turned to his trusted lieutenant as coach of Chennai Super Kings, a team that has struggled to hit its customary heights over the last three seasons, failing to make the playoffs each time.After Stephen Fleming’s exit as CSK coach, there was considerable speculation over his successor. The management left the decision largely to Dhoni. Several names were discussed, including Hemang Badani, but one understands that the former captain’s comfort level with Zaheer was among the key factors behind the former left-arm pacer landing the job.Dhoni, as captain, had famously referred to Zaheer as the Sachin Tendulkar of bowling during India’s difficult 2012 World T20 campaign in Sri Lanka.“Dhoni obviously plays a key role in our decision-making process. He, along with captain Ruturaj Gaikwad and other members of the cricket committee, concluded that Zaheer is the best man for the job,” CSK managing director Kasi Viswanathan told TOI.CSK have struggled with their pace bowling lately, particularly at the death, and Zaheer’s mastery of reverse swing also worked in his favour.“Zaheer was a world-class bowler and has mentored many young cricketers, especially fast bowlers, over the years. As a player, he was one of the key reasons for India’s success during the 2000s,” Viswanathan added.Zaheer, on his part, said it was “an honour to be part of one of the most successful teams in the history of the IPL”.“As a cricketer, I have faced CSK on the field and thoroughly enjoyed those contests. I can’t wait to join this legacy franchise with such a rich history,” he said.The 47-year-old, who represented three IPL franchises (RCB, MI and DD) during his playing career, is no stranger to coaching.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs Japan Live Score, T20I: Toss delayed due to wet outfield
articles.summary: India vs Japan Live Score, T20I: India’s one-off T20I against Japan is more than an unusual fixture on the international calendar. It carries echoes
articles.body:
Facing Jasprit Bumrah is a daunting proposition for any batter. For Japan, it will also be a unique opportunity.

India have been carefully managing Bumrah’s workload, but the fast bowler has shown that he wants more game time, including his appearance in the dead rubber against Afghanistan. Now he could take the ball against Japan.

For Japan captain Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming and the rest of the batting line-up, facing Bumrah could provide an experience few international cricketers get. His variations, accuracy and pace will test Japan at a level they rarely encounter. It is a difficult challenge, but also a memorable one.

articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur's India eye Asian Games gold repeat as they face Sri Lanka in final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Nagoya: In the almost three weeks of the Asian Games, the Indian women’s cricket team got a one-week window and three matches to win the title.With cr.
articles.body: Nagoya: In the almost three weeks of the Asian Games, the Indian women’s cricket team got a one-week window and three matches to win the title.With cricket still relatively unknown in the region, the players have been able to explore the city and its surroundings without attracting attention, from visiting the Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples of Kyoto, Japan’s cultural capital, to strolling through the streets of Nagoya. They have sampled local food, shopped and even found a taste of home at a Japanese-run Indian restaurant.At the Karogi Athletics Park cricket facility on the outskirts of the city, teams like Japan and Malaysia have rushed to meet India’s cricketers. For many of them, it’s a dream come true to meet icons like skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana. The Indian diaspora, too, has come out in large numbers.Amid all the new experiences, they haven’t lost focus on the job at hand: to retain the gold.India hardly broke a sweat in the run-up to the final. However, Sri Lanka can be tricky customers, although India beat them in the Asia Cup less than two weeks ago.The battle for gold will be a repeat of the previous edition’s final, in which India got the better of the Lankans by 19 runs in a low-scoring final.That said, Sri Lanka have been in top form en route to the finale, registering wins against Malaysia and Pakistan. Skipper Chamari Athapaththu has led from the front with 146 runs from two matches, including two half-centuries. The 36-year-old cricketer is keen to make amends for the group-stage exit in the T20 World Cup and the Asia Cup runners-up finish.While the fancied Indians will settle for nothing but gold, the opposition is not being taken lightly.“Chamari is in good form. We know that she is one of their best players, so we have plans for her. That said, we will just try to execute our own plans,” opener Shafali Verma said.There’s a prediction of rain, so both teams will also have an eye on the weather. If the match is abandoned, India, who are the top seeds, will be declared winners.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
